office_does: The County Clerk is the Superior Court's administrative and financial officer, keeping every court case record and handling case-related deposits and disbursements.
race_blurb: Sixteen-year Clerk Scott Weber, recommended by The Columbian, faces mediator and attorney Rachel Shapiro in a race The Columbian describes as a debate over court technology costs and help for people who file without a lawyer.

candidates.summary: Clark County Clerk since 2010, running on his record of keeping court records independent, accessible and digitized.
highlights: Says his independent imaging system kept the court running during the 2024 statewide system outage [S1]
Cites better restitution collection for crime victims, real-time document access and e-filing [S1]
Says the clerk must be independent to protect the integrity of court records [S1]
Recommended by The Columbian's editorial board for the general election [S7]

experience.basis: Four-term, 16-year incumbent running on his administrative and technology record.

candidates.summary: Divorce mediator and law graduate running to replace duplicative court technology and expand help for people navigating the courthouse without a lawyer.
highlights: Would replace the county's OnBase imaging system with the state-provided Odyssey system to cut costs [S5]
Proposes a courthouse legal aid department and a Lawyer of the Day program, funded mainly by grants and partners [S6][S7]
Supports a dispute-resolution center and mediation in suitable family-law cases [S4][S8]
Would hold monthly open office hours and post budget information online [S1]
Recommended by the Clark County Democratic Party [S10]

experience.basis: Never held public office beyond precinct committee officer; challenges a 16-year incumbent while stressing her legal and mediation background.

spending.basis: Pairs cutting duplicative technology costs with new courthouse access programs funded mainly by grants and partners.
